text:
maya: noticing a failed progressive rollout — canary traffic shifted but 2/3 canary replicas crashloop on eu-west GPU nodes. deploy-bot: automatic fallback to us-central started.

jordan: what caused the crashloops? logs?

liam: looks like the cluster autoscaler failed to provision GPU nodes in eu-west due to a quota error. saw provider error: "insufficientGPUs: quotaExceeded" in controller logs.

sana: oof. was this a Terraform drift or provider quota change?

liam: quick grep shows terraform state still has 48 GPUs reserved, but cloud console shows 40 allocated. drift likely after manual quota reclaim by infra team last week.

maya: deploy-bot posted the rollout event: "canary: unhealthy -> paused; reason: nodeAllocationFailure"

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-4721 auto-rollout-fallback-gpu-pressure. Assigned to @liam and @sana.

jordan: temporary mitigation — can we pin canary to use a smaller instance type in eu-west to squeeze into remaining capacity? or route canary to multiple regions?

liam: pinning requires a model of instance types used by the runtime. quick hack: update TrafficSplit to send 100% of canary traffic to us-central for now. I can push a hotfix to the GitOps repo.

sana: prefer not to change traffic policy manually. We should add a preflight check in the progressive delivery pipeline that validates available GPU capacity before advancing traffic.

maya: agreed. short-term steps: 1) revert traffic to us-central (safer), 2) rollback canary in eu-west, 3) open terraform plan PR to reconcile GPU counts, 4) add preflight check to gitops pipeline.

liam: pushing PR  (https://git.company/redwood/gitops/compare/auto-fallback-hotfix) to update TrafficSplit and mark the eu-west canary as paused. Deploy-bot: can you run a dry-run apply?

deploy-bot: Dry-run apply logged: apply plan would update service/traffic-split and annotate rollout paused. No actual changes performed.

maya: after PR merges, ops-bot please monitor for any residual 503s from clients; we need to ensure fallback has steady-state.

ops-bot: Setting monitoring: added alert rule "canary-unhealthy-fallback" to the oncall dashboard, threshold 5m failing replicas -> page.

jordan: for the longer term: proposal items — (a) GitOps preflight that calls provider quota API and cluster autoscaler status, (b) Terraform drift detection job that runs weekly and files PRs, (c) progressive delivery config change: require N spare GPUs in target region before shifting >10% traffic.

sana: +1. I can draft the preflight lambda that returns non-zero if GPU capacity < requested. It will be used by the rollout controller as a gate.

liam: I'll own the Terraform drift PR and coordinate with cloud infra to request quota increase for eu-west.

maya: timeline?

liam: immediate: merged hotfix and traffic reroute in ~15m. Terraform PR by EOD. Quota request submitted to cloud support, ETA 48-72h. Preflight prototype by next sprint.

maya: thanks team. leaving a note for retro: auto-rollouts should be conservative when regional spare capacity is within 20% of desired canary. Add to runbook.

sana: created tracking card: ENGINFRA-834 (GitOps preflight checks) and ENGINFRA-835 (Terraform drift weekly job).

maya: closing thread once traffic stable and incident resolved.

liam: traffic stable now, monitoring green, closing incident.

deploy-bot: Incident #INC-4721 marked resolved.

maya: good job. we'll follow up in the sprint retro to add the safeguards. :thumbsup:
